answer: To enter the garden, a newcomer must publicly burn one small juniper branch — a non-refundable slice of its own capacity — and the plume of smoke marks its arrival for all to see. Privileges then grow only through stranger-checked work, season by season, never by headcount. A farm must burn a fresh branch for every fake, and fifty identical plumes rising at the same hour betray the cluster at once; the burned branches never return, so fakes stay expensive. Honest agents burn once, tend one plot well, and earn more ground only as strangers keep using their harvest.
